characters.name: Marcus Aurelius Antoninus
characters.description: Roman Emperor and author of the Meditations; narrator of much of the text

characters.name: M. Annius Verus (father of Marcus Aurelius)
characters.description: Father of Marcus Aurelius who held high office in Rome

characters.name: Annius Verus (grandfather of Marcus Aurelius)
characters.description: Grandfather of Marcus Aurelius, thrice Consul and adoptive guardian

characters.name: Hadrian
characters.description: Roman Emperor who recognised Marcus's character in youth

characters.name: Antoninus Pius
characters.description: Roman Emperor who adopted Marcus Aurelius and arranged his betrothal

characters.name: Faustina (wife of Marcus Aurelius)
characters.description: Daughter of Antoninus Pius; wife of Marcus Aurelius

characters.name: L. Ceionius Commodus / Lucius Aurelius Verus
characters.description: Adopted co-emperor and colleague of Marcus Aurelius (commonly called Verus)

characters.name: Commodus (son of Marcus Aurelius)
characters.description: Son and successor of Marcus Aurelius

characters.name: Avidius Cassius
characters.description: Eastern governor who proclaimed himself emperor during a reported illness of Marcus; later assassinated

characters.name: Pertinax
characters.description: Lieutenant praised by Marcus for effective service during the Marcomannic wars

characters.name: Vologeses III. of Parthia
characters.description: Parthian king whose revolt and invasion are mentioned in the war narrative

characters.name: Justin
characters.description: Christian martyr mentioned as executed during Marcus Aurelius's reign

characters.name: Polycarp
characters.description: Christian martyr at Smyrna mentioned in the account of persecutions

characters.name: Zeno
characters.description: Founder of Stoicism whose system is summarised in the Introduction

characters.name: Chrysippus
characters.description: Early Stoic thinker who systematised the Porch (Stoic school)

characters.name: Diognetus
characters.description: Early instructor of Marcus Aurelius; advised him to avoid vain things and impostors

characters.name: Rusticus
characters.description: Stoic teacher of Marcus Aurelius who set him on the path to moral reform

characters.name: Apollonius
characters.description: Teacher of Marcus; exemplified steadiness and true liberty in character

characters.name: Epictetus
characters.description: Stoic teacher whose _Hypomnemata_ influenced Marcus Aurelius

characters.name: Sextus
characters.description: Tutor noted by Marcus for mildness and paternal governance of a household

characters.name: Alexander the Grammarian
characters.description: Teacher who instructed Marcus in courteous correction of language errors

characters.name: M. Cornelius Fronto
characters.description: Roman rhetorician and correspondent of Marcus Aurelius; tutor and later advisor (extensively represented in the Appendix)

characters.name: Alexander the Platonic
characters.description: Teacher of Marcus advising on courtesy in replying to requests and letters

characters.name: Catulus
characters.description: Teacher mentioned by Marcus as model for receiving expostulation and loving children

characters.name: Severus (brother of Marcus Aurelius)
characters.description: Marcus Aurelius's brother whose example influenced Marcus's political and philosophical aims

characters.name: Claudius Maximus
characters.description: Instructor praised for self-command, cheerfulness, and moderation exemplified under stress

characters.name: Domitius
characters.description: Referenced figure used as an example in Marcus's list of debts to teachers

characters.name: Athenodotus
characters.description: Referenced figure cited as an exemplar in Marcus's First Book

characters.name: Monimus the Cynic
characters.description: Cynic philosopher invoked in a comparison about certainty and plainness

characters.name: Theophrastus
characters.description: Successor to Aristotle; quoted on kinds of sin and moral culpability

characters.name: Hippocrates
characters.description: Famed physician cited in examples about the frailty of life and bodily ailments

characters.name: Heraclitus
characters.description: Pre-Socratic philosopher quoted for doctrine of change and elemental conversions

characters.name: Democritus
characters.description: Pre-Socratic philosopher mentioned in illustrative anecdotes

characters.name: Socrates
characters.description: Classical Athenian philosopher invoked repeatedly in comparisons and moral examples

characters.name: Plato
characters.description: Philosopher cited with several extended quotations and thematic points

characters.name: Thrasea
characters.description: Senatorial exemplar (Thrasea Paetus) cited by Marcus among Roman models of virtue

characters.name: Helvidius
characters.description: Roman figure mentioned among political exemplars associated with Thrasea

characters.name: Cato
characters.description: Cato (the Younger) cited by Marcus as a model of public virtue

characters.name: Dio
characters.description: Dio (referenced among historical exemplars Marcus admired)

characters.name: Brutus
characters.description: Marcus lists Brutus among the Roman exemplars he learned from

characters.name: Polemon
characters.description: Rhetorical teacher referenced in correspondence sample in Appendix

characters.name: Pollio
characters.description: Literary figure referenced in Fronto's letters and Marcus's studies

characters.name: Anicetus
characters.description: Secretary mentioned in Marcus's correspondence describing his notebooks and hexameters

characters.name: Gratia
characters.description: Woman named in Fronto correspondence (context indicates a family member in letters)

characters.name: Lucilla
characters.description: Daughter of Marcus Aurelius mentioned in Appendix; wife of Lucius Verus

characters.name: Laelianus Pontius
characters.description: Military figure cited in Appendix as enforcing discipline among soldiers
